entries.concept: valuation verdict: cheap, expensive, overvalued, undervalued
questions: is nvda too expensive right now
is kroger a bargain at this price
is intel cheap vs its history
is X trading at a discount to peers
entries.market_reading: A comparative question: is the price the market puts on the company's earnings, cash flow, sales or assets high or low against a benchmark (its own history, its peers, the market, its growth, or an estimate of intrinsic value). The share price alone never answers it; the market's answer is always 'cheap or expensive relative to B on multiple M', usually on more than one multiple.

figures.notes: us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss is attributable to the parent (after noncontrolling interests) but before preferred dividends. Never use us-gaap:ProfitLoss for P/E: it includes the noncontrolling interests' share. 10-Q income-statement facts come as both the quarter and year-to-date: read each fact's own start and end dates.

figures.notes: Excluding versus including assessed (excise, sales) taxes changes the level. 10-Q revenue facts come as both the quarter and year-to-date: read each fact's own start and end dates. | element notes: us-gaap:SalesRevenueNet (pre-2018 filings; absent from the 2026 taxonomy) ; banks: us-gaap:RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense, or us-gaap:InterestIncomeExpenseNet + us-gaap:NoninterestIncome

figures.notes: 10-Q cash-flow statements are fiscal year-to-date only; there is no discrete-quarter cash-flow statement.

figures.name: common shareholders' equity (book value)
figures.sign: positive; negative equity makes P/B not meaningful
figures.notes: us-gaap:StockholdersEquity is attributable to the parent (excludes noncontrolling interests). Subtract preferred held in permanent equity to get common book: take us-gaap:PreferredStockIncludingAdditionalPaidInCapital (the issuance value), else us-gaap:PreferredStockValue, which FASB defines as the aggregate par or stated value only and which includes treasury shares. us-gaap:PreferredStockLiquidationPreferenceValue is not the liquidation preference: FASB defines it as the excess of the preference over par or stated value. Where an analyst wants the preference itself, add that excess to the par or stated value. Read the equity note and record which basis was used. Never use us-gaap:StockholdersEquityIncludingPortionAttributableToNoncontrollingInterest for P/B.

entries.formula: Pick the multiple(s) the market uses for this kind of business (EV/EBITDA or EV/EBIT and P/E for operating companies; P/E, P/B, P/TBV for banks and insurers; P/FFO for REITs; price/NAV for BDCs and closed-end funds; EV/Sales for unprofitable companies), compute each on a consistent basis, then place it in one or more frames and report the comparison (e.g. 'P/E 18 vs own 5-year median 24 and peer median 21'), not a bare verdict.
entries.period_convention: Flows (earnings, EBITDA, revenue, cash flow) on a trailing-twelve-month basis: latest fiscal year + current fiscal year-to-date - the prior year's same year-to-date (10-Q cash-flow facts are year-to-date only; 10-Q income-statement facts come as both the quarter and year-to-date, so read each fact's own start and end dates; Q4 = full year - nine-month YTD). Balance-sheet items at the latest balance-sheet date. Price on a stated date on or after the filing that supplied the fundamentals. Trend = the same multiple re-computed at each past date with the price and fundamentals known then.
entries.frame_notes: history: the multiple against the company's own multi-year median or range. peers: against the median (or harmonic mean) of comparable companies in the same industry, same fiscal calendar after calendarising. market: against a broad index multiple (index data are licensed; relative P/E = company P/E / index P/E). growth-adjusted: PEG or justified multiples that control for growth, risk and payout. intrinsic: DCF or other present-value estimate against the price. yield-comparison: earnings, FCF or dividend yield against government bond yields. absolute: practitioner rules of thumb (Graham's P/E 15 and P/B 1.5, PEG 1), which no authority draws.
entries.direction: depends: for price multiples (P/E, EV/EBITDA, P/B, P/S) lower = cheaper; for yields (earnings, FCF, dividend) higher = cheaper. Cheaper is not better: a low multiple can reflect low growth, high risk or falling earnings (a value trap), and a high multiple can reflect expected growth.

thresholds.line: estimated intrinsic value above price = undervalued; about equal = fairly valued; below price = overvalued (CFA's three states)
thresholds.meaning: the textbook definition of mispricing; says nothing about how the intrinsic value was estimated

pitfalls: Answering from the share price level or a price fall alone.
Mixing equity and enterprise measures (e.g. market cap / EBITDA, or EV / net income).
Negative or near-zero denominators: report 'not meaningful', not a huge or negative multiple.
One-off items in trailing earnings; GAAP versus company-adjusted earnings (vendors often use adjusted).
Peers with different fiscal year ends compared without calendarising.
Sector-inappropriate multiples (EV multiples for banks; P/E for REITs).
Stale price against new fundamentals, or a new price against stale fundamentals.

entries.concept: enterprise value (EV)
questions: how much debt is in X's enterprise value
whats the takeover value of X
why is X's EV bigger than its market cap
entries.market_reading: The value of the operating business to all capital providers: the price a buyer would pay for the equity plus the debt and other senior claims it takes on, less the cash it gets. It is the numerator for the capital-structure-neutral multiples (EV/EBITDA, EV/EBIT, EV/Sales).

figures.name: share price (market input)
figures.notes: Not carried by any filing as a daily series. Needs a dated closing price from a licensed exchange or consolidated feed (see VA-25). Record the price date next to the share-count date.

figures.name: common shares outstanding (cover page)
figures.notes: Cover value is as of a 'latest practicable date' shortly before filing, i.e. after the period end; one fact per class (dimension us-gaap:StatementClassOfStockAxis), so sum the classes. The balance-sheet fallback is as of the period end. dei is the SEC's taxonomy: cite the name as an identifier.

figures.name: total debt (borrowings and finance leases)
figures.notes: A composition, not one tag. LongTermDebt usually includes current maturities, so LongTermDebt + LongTermDebtCurrent double counts. us-gaap:DebtCurrent is FASB's debt and lease obligation classified as current: it can already hold current maturities and short-term borrowings, and it includes current lease obligations. Never add us-gaap:LongTermDebtCurrent, us-gaap:FinanceLeaseLiability or current lease liabilities to it; when leases are summed separately, use us-gaap:LongTermDebtCurrent (which excludes lease obligations) + us-gaap:ShortTermBorrowings instead of DebtCurrent. Record which parts were summed. Carrying (book) amounts, not market values.

figures.name: preferred stock
figures.notes: Redeemable preferred sits in temporary (mezzanine) equity, outside StockholdersEquity; perpetual preferred sits inside it. Temporary equity can hold other redeemable instruments too: check the note. Permanent-equity figure: us-gaap:PreferredStockIncludingAdditionalPaidInCapital (issuance value, issued and outstanding) where tagged; else us-gaap:PreferredStockValue, which FASB defines as aggregate par or stated value only and which includes treasury stock, so it is a floor and not the claim. Temporary-equity figure: us-gaap:TemporaryEquityCarryingAmountAttributableToParent (carrying amount). Neither carrying figure is the liquidation or redemption claim. The fallbacks us-gaap:PreferredStockLiquidationPreferenceValue and us-gaap:TemporaryEquityLiquidationPreference are, by FASB's documentation, the excess of the liquidation preference over par or stated value, not the preferred claim; each can understate the claim, down to zero when the preference equals par. Some filers tag the full preference with these elements anyway, so read the equity or temporary-equity note before using either. For the EV claim, take the aggregate liquidation or redemption amount stated in the note. If the note does not state it, answer 'could not establish'.

figures.name: noncontrolling interests
figures.notes: Standard label 'Equity, Attributable to Noncontrolling Interest'. Added to EV because consolidated EBITDA and revenue include 100% of partly owned subsidiaries.

figures.name: cash and short-term investments
figures.notes: Restricted cash is not free to pay claims. Short-term investment tags can overlap: do not add two that contain each other. | element notes: us-gaap:CashCashEquivalentsRestrictedCashAndRestrictedCashEquivalents (includes restricted cash; remove us-gaap:RestrictedCashAndCashEquivalents)

figures.name: operating lease liabilities
figures.notes: On the balance sheet since ASC 842. Include in EV only when the denominator is before lease cost (add back us-gaap:OperatingLeaseCost: EBITDAR). | element notes: us-gaap:OperatingLeaseLiabilityCurrent + us-gaap:OperatingLeaseLiabilityNoncurrent

figures.name: equity-method investments
figures.notes: Non-operating asset in fuller EV builds; its income (us-gaap:IncomeLossFromEquityMethodInvestments) sits outside EBITDA.

figures.name: defined benefit plan funded status
figures.notes: Optional debt-like claim in fuller EV builds; usually only in the annual pension note. The primary is signed negative = underfunded; the fallback us-gaap:DefinedBenefitPensionPlanLiabilitiesNoncurrent is a recognised liability reported as a positive amount, so negate it to match the funded-status sign, or add it to EV directly.

entries.formula: Equity market value + total debt (short- and long-term borrowings, current maturities, finance leases) + preferred stock + noncontrolling interests - cash and cash equivalents - short-term investments. Fuller builds add operating lease liabilities (only with a pre-rent denominator such as EBITDAR) and unfunded pensions, and subtract non-operating assets such as equity-method investments.
entries.period_convention: Point in time: equity value at the price date; debt, cash, preferred and NCI from the latest balance sheet (state both dates).
entries.frame_notes: EV is a level, not a ratio; it is judged only inside a multiple (VA-09 to VA-11) or against a deal price.
entries.direction: neither: a level

thresholds.line: EV < 0
thresholds.meaning: market cap is below net cash (cash exceeds market cap plus debt and other claims)

figures.name: diluted EPS
figures.notes: Reported per class under the two-class method for multi-class issuers. 10-Q facts can be the quarter or year-to-date: select by context duration. Later filings restate prior EPS for stock splits. | element notes: us-gaap:EarningsPerShareBasicAndDiluted (older filings; absent from the 2026 taxonomy) ; us-gaap:IncomeLossFromContinuingOperationsPerDilutedShare (continuing operations only)

figures.notes: us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss is attributable to the parent (after noncontrolling interests) but before preferred dividends. Never use us-gaap:ProfitLoss for P/E: it includes the noncontrolling interests' share. 10-Q income-statement facts come as both the quarter and year-to-date: read each fact's own start and end dates.

entries.formula: Price / trailing-twelve-month diluted EPS; equivalently market cap / TTM net income available to common. Negative or near-zero earnings: report 'not meaningful' (NM).
entries.period_convention: Flows (earnings, EBITDA, revenue, cash flow) on a trailing-twelve-month basis: latest fiscal year + current fiscal year-to-date - the prior year's same year-to-date (10-Q cash-flow facts are year-to-date only; 10-Q income-statement facts come as both the quarter and year-to-date, so read each fact's own start and end dates; Q4 = full year - nine-month YTD). Balance-sheet items at the latest balance-sheet date. Price on a stated date on or after the filing that supplied the fundamentals. Trend = the same multiple re-computed at each past date with the price and fundamentals known then. Do not sum four quarterly EPS figures blindly: share counts change; TTM net income / latest diluted share count or market cap / TTM net income is cleaner.
entries.frame_notes: history: against its own 5-10 year median. peers: against the industry median or harmonic mean. market: relative P/E against an index P/E. growth-adjusted: PEG (VA-08). yield-comparison: earnings yield against bond yields (VA-07). absolute: Graham's P/E ceiling of 15 is a practitioner rule, not a line any authority draws.
entries.direction: lower = cheaper, all else equal; a high P/E may reflect expected growth and a low one expected decline

entries.concept: forward price-to-earnings ratio
questions: is X cheap on forward earnings

entries.market_reading: Price divided by expected earnings per share for the next twelve months or the next fiscal year, as forecast by analysts (consensus) or, less often, by management guidance. Equity-level variants discount dividends (DDM) or free cash flow to equity at the cost of equity.

figures.name: preferred stock
figures.notes: Redeemable preferred sits in temporary (mezzanine) equity, outside StockholdersEquity; perpetual preferred sits inside it. notes: 1) Every valuation multiple is a market price (not in filings) set against a filed fundamental. So measurable_from_filings is false for every price-based entry, and true only for the filed halves: public float (VA-03) and book or tangible book per share (VA-15). EPS, EBITDA inputs, FCF, net debt, NCAV and NAV per share are measurable inside the other entries. 2) Price sources, plainly: the official close is the listing exchange's (NYSE closing auction; Nasdaq Official Closing Price) and is licensed proprietary data. NYSE requires a licence even for delayed feeds. The consolidated tape (SIP) is sold under CTA and UTP plan fee schedules. The SEC dropped 10-K price tables in 2018 because prices are free to view online, but free to view is not public domain. No public-domain daily closing-price series for US equities was found. The nearest government-published price is the SEC fails-to-deliver file (public-domain licence label on its data.gov catalog entry; only securities with a recorded fails balance), a candidate for checking, not a series. Filings carry sparse dated prices: public float, Item 703 average repurchase price, Item 402 grant-date close and TSR, and Form 4 transaction prices. Admitting any price source is an owner decision under rules 4 and 18 and; Nasdaq and vendor pages stay finding-and-checking only. 3) Consistency principle (Damodaran; CFA): equity multiples pair market cap with equity-level flows (net income available to common, levered FCF, common book). EV multiples pair EV with firm-level flows (EBITDA, EBIT, revenue, unlevered FCF). Every claim added to EV needs a matching denominator: NCI goes with 100%-consolidated EBITDA, operating leases with EBITDAR, and removing equity-method investments with excluding their income. 4) Periods: 10-Q flows are fiscal year-to-date. TTM = latest FY + current YTD - prior-year YTD, and Q4 = FY - 9M. Calendarise peers with different fiscal years. An SEC proposal of May 2026 (Form 10-S, semiannual reporting) is not adopted. If adopted, some filers would have half-year interims only. 5) Share counts: the cover-page dei count (a date after period end, per class, so sum the classes), the balance-sheet count (period end), the weighted-average basic and diluted counts (period averages) and public float (dollars, second-quarter end) are five different things. Use a point-in-time count for market cap and diluted weighted shares for EPS. 6) Element traps (checked against FASB's 2026 taxonomy): us-gaap:NetIncomeLoss is attributable to the parent while us-gaap:ProfitLoss includes NCI. us-gaap:StockholdersEquity excludes NCI. us-gaap:DepreciationAndAmortization is nonproduction D&A only. SalesRevenueNet, EarningsPerShareBasicAndDiluted and TreasuryStockShares are absent from the 2026 taxonomy but appear in older filings. There is no us-gaap EBITDA, FCF or FFO element: all three are non-GAAP (Reg G, Item 10(e)). 7) Repo check: 'ev' omits preferred stock and noncontrolling interests. 'pe' uses net_income, which falls back to us-gaap:ProfitLoss (includes NCI). 'cash' falls back to a tag that includes restricted cash. 'stockholders_equity' falls back to a tag that includes NCI. 'buyback_yield' is gross. 'bvps' divides balance-sheet equity by a cover-date share count. These are consistency gaps against VA-04, VA-05, VA-13, VA-15 and VA-19. 8) Thresholds: no authority draws a cheap or expensive line. The only source-drawn lines in the family are the SEC filer-status lines on public float ($75m, $250m, $700m), and they are not valuation lines. Every numeric valuation line recorded here is a practitioner rule of thumb: Graham's P/E 15, P/B 1.5, 22.5 and two-thirds of NCAV; PEG 1; the Fed model; terminal growth no higher than the risk-free rate; a 10-15% conglomerate discount; and size buckets that differ by source. The rest are definitional: below book, below NCAV, EV below zero, and price below NAV. 9) Sector fit: banks and insurers use P/E, P/B and P/TBV (EV multiples do not apply). REITs use P/FFO, P/AFFO and NAV. BDCs and closed-end funds use price/NAV. Unprofitable growers use EV/Sales. Capital-intensive firms use EV/EBIT or FCF alongside EV/EBITDA. 10) DCF, intrinsic value, implied growth and price targets are opinions or model outputs, never filed facts. Under project rules 5 and 17 they are labelled proposals, or the answer is 'could not establish'. For 'is X undervalued' with no licensed price, a Case answer can give the filed half and name the missing input. 11) Source ids are global across entries (same id = same source); S-numbers with gaps are intentional. Quotes appear only on US-government public-domain pages fetched in this run. Each was checked word for word against a local copy of the fetched page. Numeric practitioner claims (size buckets, Graham's 15, 1.5 and 22.5 and two-thirds, PEG 1, CAPE 15-16, the 10-15% conglomerate discount, Damodaran's growth caps, 5-10 year forecasts) were re-checked in the raw page text, and two claims that a fetch-tool summary had added were dropped (a 2-4% terminal-growth range; a twice-monthly publication frequency).
